title: Efficacy of conbercept pro re nata (PRN) versus treat-and-extend (T&E) regimens following five initial monthly doses in diabetic macular edema: a 24-month retrospective cohort study

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY))

condition: Newly diagnosed, treatment-naive diabetic macular edema in type 2 diabetes (CFT >= 300 µm; no prior PRP, intravitreal anti-VEGF/steroid or vitrectomy); single-centre retrospective cohort (Qilu Hospital, Shandong University), 119 eyes of 119 patients treated September 2020 to September 2022 with at least 24 months of regular follow-up

groups.description: 5+PRN: five initial monthly conbercept injections, then 4-weekly evaluation with reinjection when predefined retreatment criteria were met
5+T&E: five initial monthly conbercept injections, then treat-and-extend starting at 8 weeks (shortened to a minimum of 4 weeks or extended by 4 weeks up to 16 weeks)

series.notes: Mean ± SD (Methods: normally distributed data as mean ± SD; the 24m cells print the SD without the ± sign); scheduled 6/12/18/24-month visits with a ±4-week window (nominal times); completers with regular follow-up (patients lost to follow-up excluded)
Mean ± SD; same visit windows and completer definition as the 5+PRN series

exclusions.what: Table 3 F, P, t and P rows/columns
exclusions.reason: test statistics and p-values are not admissible
duplicates the Table 3 baseline cells (same eyes); Table 3 cited

exclusions.what: Tables 2 and 4-9 (BCVA, microaneurysm count, venular diameter, DCP vessel density, FAZ area, hard exudate and haemorrhage area categories)
exclusions.reason: not retinal thickness (counts/proportions or other measures)

notes: Time origin: the first conbercept injection at the first visit (start of the five monthly loading doses)
CFT defined in the Methods as the perpendicular ILM to inner-RPE distance at the foveal centre on a single cross-sectional Cirrus HD-OCT scan: measure central_point, device cirrus

Regimen groups were allocated after the loading phase according to practical conditions and treatment preferences (geographical accessibility, feasibility of regular visits), not randomised and not by a post-baseline outcome; both groups received identical treatment until the end of loading
Rescue PRP was permitted for neovascularization; PRP was given after loading to 6 (5+PRN) and 10 (5+T&E) patients with neovascularization present at baseline FFA; no values were removed or replaced
Means are over eyes with complete follow-up (inclusion required at least 24 months of regular follow-up; data within ±4 weeks of each scheduled visit accepted)
